title: Pre-Market: Tue Nov 3, 2026 (Election Day)
html:
Headline: Apple and Palantir drag, chips bounce, and SPY sits on the line.

The one thing

SPY is at $751.42 pre-market, just under the $752.30 line (38.2% + 1.0× extension). Whether it reclaims the line or slides toward $743–745 in the first hour sets the tone. The midterms and AMD's report both come after the bell.

Overnight

  • Futures: S&P −0.1% to −0.2%, Nasdaq-100 +0.1% to +0.2%, Dow −0.7% to −0.9% (Apple).
  • Asia: Japan closed for a holiday. Kospi down more than 3% (Samsung and SK Hynix about −5%). Hang Seng edged up.
  • Oil: WTI about $98.50 (+2.1%), Brent about $106.50 (+1.7%), after a reported US strike on Qeshm Island.
  • 10-year yield about 4.89%. VIX about 21.6.

SPY game plan

  • Above $752.30 and holding through 10:00 → $763.50–767 ceiling in play. No SPY calls until a close above $767.
  • Between $743 and $752 → chop, wait.
  • Below $743 → defense, $734 next.

Movers on the Watchlist

  • AAPL $324.92 (−4.0%): weak margin outlook. Don't buy the gap.
  • PLTR $166.46 (−6.7%): near the $163–165 zone. Wait a day or two.
  • NVDA $205.45 (+1.7%): chip bounce (MU +3.8%, SMH +2.3%, DRAM +3.1%). Put trigger further away.
  • AMD $480.31 (+2.9%), SMCI $31.15 (+2.3%): report tonight. IV crush risk.
  • BE $208.65 (+6.3%): near the $210.84 ceiling.
  • Ideas: HLT $364.00, RCL $318.00, DAL $82.99. No levels broken.

Calendar (ET)

  • 10:00: JOLTS (7.1M expected), factory orders (about +1.1%).
  • After the close: AMD and SMCI earnings, election results, API crude at 4:30.
  • No Fed speakers found. Next FOMC Dec 8–9.

Plays check (Options Playbook)

  • HLT Dec 18 $380 call: still valid, closer. Close above $364.50 today = second close. Stop: close below $352.
  • DAL Dec 18 $85 call: wait. Trigger: close above $85.40. Cancel: close below $80.90, or oil over $100.
  • NVDA Dec 18 $190 put: wait, leaning off. Off on a close above $205. On again on a close below $200.

Opening rule

Wait for the 10:00 JOLTS number and the first 30-minute candle. Use limit orders.

Educational, not personal investment advice. Claude never places trades.
